newsitem.title: FRANCE: Extradited Iranian held for murder in France.
newsitem.headline: Extradited Iranian held for murder in France.

text.p: A French court began the formal investigation on Friday of Iranian Ahmad Jeyhouni, who has been extradited from Germany as a suspected accomplice in the murder of former Iranian minister Reza Mazlouman.
Jeyhouni, 61, a resident of Bonn arrested soon after the killing last May, was flow to Paris on Thursday evening.

Judge Jean-Francois Ricard remanded him in custody and told him was being formally probed as an accomplice to the murder of Mazlouman, a vice-minister of education under the late Shah before the 1979 Islamic revolution.
French media say Jeyhouni ran a video cassette shop in Bonn, and that he had been identified by a woman friend of Mazlouman as having visited him just before the killing in Paris last May.

The French investigation is being led by anti-terrorism judge Jean-Louis Bruguiere, who investigated the murder of the Shah's last prime minister, Shapour Bakhtiar, in France in 1991. Several Iranians were convicted of the murder two years ago.
Since the 1979 revolution, eight Iranian exiles have been killed in France and several dozen in other countries.

Iranian resistance officials say Tehran was behind the murders, and allege that the Iranian embassy in Bonn houses a coordination centre for attacks on dissidents living in Europe. Iran has always denied involvement in such attacks.
